title: FLA writer: timeline-write truncates Page N stream for very short layer names (e.g. 'L')
description: DONE. Root cause: writeCPicFrame (packages/core/src/fla/write/timeline-write.ts) stamped frame schema fs=0x18 but stopped after the tweenInstanceName BomString, omitting the mandatory F8 frame-tail: fs>19 skip(4), fs>20 skip(4), fs>=22 skip(4), and the fs>=24 ease-curve header (u32 useSingleEaseCurve; u32 hasCustomEase) = 20 bytes total. The reader (readCPicFrameNode in flash8-binary.ts) consumes those 20 bytes for fs=0x18, so it over-read the frame body by exactly 20 bytes and the following CPicLayer name/trailer parsed off-by-20. The corruption looked layer-name-length-dependent (1-char 'L' truncated, 7-char 'Layer 1' fell back to default reconstruction) only because the off-by-20 landed on different bytes per name length; the actual field at fault is the frame schema-tail, NOT the layer-name BomString. The empty-keyframe path was unaffected because PAGE_FRAME_BODY (the genuine fixture body) already carries the full tail; only the full-serialization path (sound-bearing or non-empty keyframes) hit it. Fix: append the 5 u32 fields (values 1/0/0/1/0, verbatim from the genuine flash8-empty.fla PAGE_FRAME_BODY tail; hasCustomEase=0 since easing is the s16 acceleration field). Verify: full ordered build green; full core suite 5550 passed/8 skipped (empty-bytematch SKIP is the 1207 fixture gate, not a failure); added 19 round-trip regressions (real-fla-write.test.ts: 1-char L, edge lengths La/Lay/AB/ABCD/ABCDE/ABCDEF, Layer 1, 40-char, through both parseFla8Timeline and tryLoadRealFla with frame-sound link rebuilt + no parse warnings, plus a strict-CArchive-valid shape frame with 1-char name). Frame.sound / media-catalog / writer-spec-bytes / carchive-validate all still pass. Doc: clarified docs/21 §11 that the F8 ease-curve header is mandatory when fs=0x18.
